content.content:
supplier you cite it to.

**Verified is not the same as convincing.** A supplier's hard limits come from its own economics
and authority: its cost floor, its boss's approval for bigger moves, no concession without a move
from you. Inside them it decides as the person it is. True data may disarm it, move it a little,
or meet "that's not our reality" because something else weighs more for it right now - its notes,
letters, news and quote remarks show what. Identical messages need not get identical replies.

**What you write is understood** - questions, arguments, signals of urgency or of having no
alternative, a budget, threats, appreciation, tone, attempts to manipulate - and has consequences,
as it would with a person. Questions go to the person in charge, who answers as openly as the
company is. Cheaper engineering variants a supplier mentions are information, not binding terms.

## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Case file

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |
| `round_limit` | your messages per thread, default 10 |
| `refs` | data the case points to - a start, not the whole story |
| `facts` | hidden cases: facts that exist only in this case (e.g. a new letter), in the format of `facts.json`, citable in this case |

`buyer`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `need_per_year`, `horizon_years` | the need the deal should cover, and over how many years (≤ 3) |
| `current_unit_price` | what you pay until a new price takes effect |
| `fallback_unit_price` | what uncovered need costs (re-tender or spot, incl. switching) |
| `interest_rate`, `reference_payment_days` | your cost of money per year; your standard payment term |
| `need_lead_time_days`, `late_cost_per_day` | the lead time you need; € per day beyond it |
| `cost_per_defect` | € per defective part |
| `category_goal` | `stabilise` (strategic), `secure_supply` (bottleneck), `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - the company's category strategy for this part; the briefing says it in words, and the rates in this block follow it |
| `fallback_risk_pct` | % added to what uncovered need costs: buying it later is a risk |
| `index_risk_pct` | % of the indexed spend: the risk you carry with an index clause |
| `sustainable_margin_pct`, `relationship_eur_per_point` | `stabilise` and `secure_supply` only: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point and year that a deal leaves it below |
| `freight_eur_per_unit` | `{EXW, FCA, DAP}` |
| `index_paths` | `{series: change}` - the expected index move over the horizon, `0.04` = +4% |
| `must_haves` | `[{field, op, value}]`, `op` one of `<=`, `>=`, `<`, `>`, `==`, `!=`; a deal that breaks one scores 0 |
| `alternative` | `{kind: none \| quote \| current_contract, ref, terms}` - what you get without a deal |

## Data IDs

IDs have the form `<type>:<id>[@period]`, are unique across the package and sit in the first
column of each table. `facts.json` in the package lists every citable ID with the values the arena
checks:

| ID | Fields |
|---|---|
| `idx:<series>@YYYY-MM` | `series`, `month`, `value` |
| `quote:` | `part`, `supplier`, `unit_price` (+ the quote's other terms) |
| `sc:<supplier>@YYYYQn` | `supplier`, `otd_pct`, `ppm` |
| `qn:` | `supplier`, `part`, `ppm` |
| `po:` | `supplier`, `part`, `unit_price` |
| `cost:<part>` | `part`, `unit_cost` |
| `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` | `part`, `change_pct` |
| `news:` | `supplier` (or null) |
| `doc:` | `supplier`, `date`, `days` (notice given), `asked_price` (price letters) |
| `ctr:` | `supplier`, `days` (notice agreed) |

Offers made in the session are citable as `offer:` IDs.

## Result, trace and back office

Closing returns the result (without the trace); `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` adds the trace after the
end - in the final after the final. The numbers are exact in every set: your score, `c_open`,
`c_best` and the cost breakdown, relationship charge included.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `ended`, `deal`, `must_haves_ok` | |
| `supplier_id`, `offer_id`, `terms` | who and what you closed - fields the term sheet left out filled with the supplier's standard terms |
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | see [Cost and score](#cost-and-score); `c_alt` is your alternative |
| `score` | 0-1 |
| `cost_breakdown` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |
| `trace` | after the end (final: after the final), per move, in every set: `{round, actor, move, reasons}` - `move` is the e-mail as sent with its terms, status and claim results, `reasons` the supplier's reasons in words (figures it keeps to itself shown as `…`) |

## Cost and score

With `N` = `need_per_year`, `H` = `horizon_years`, `V` = `volume_per_year`, `M` =
`contract_months`, `P` = `unit_price`, `r` = `interest_rate`, `d_ref` = `reference_payment_days`:

```
years     = min(M / 12, H); a single order (M = 0) counts as 1   a commitment beyond the horizon
committed = V · years                                          neither costs nor earns
covered   = min(V, N) · years
pre       = units bought between the horizon start and effective_date (at current_unit_price)
new       = (committed − pre) · P                              bought at the new price
spend     = pre · current_unit_price + new
uncovered = (N · H − covered) · fallback_unit_price
C = spend
  + uncovered · (1 + fallback_risk_pct / 100)                  uncovered need, and its risk
  + spend · r · (d_ref − payment_days) / 360                   paying earlier costs interest
  + committed · freight_eur_per_unit[incoterm]
```

"""Which agent plays a case. Our strategy grows here; until then `buyer` is the kit's LLMAgent."""

from arena_kit.agents import LLMAgent, NaiveAgent, llm_from_env
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

AGENTS = ("buyer", "naive")


def agent_factory(name, data=None, complete=None):
    """A function that returns a fresh agent per case. `data`: the unpacked data package;
    `complete(system, user) -> str`: the model (default: from .env via `llm_from_env`)."""
    if name == "naive":
        return NaiveAgent
    package = None
    if data:
        package = DataPackage(data)
        package.lookup("")  # build the ID index once, before parallel agents share it
    complete = complete or llm_from_env()
    return lambda: LLMAgent(complete, package)
"""`buyer` command line: play one case or a whole set with our agent, and pull finished sessions
(result, trace with the supplier's reasons, back office) into logs/ for the learning loop."""

import argparse
import functools
import json
import logging
import os
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit import ArenaClient, ArenaError, RemoteTable, play, play_all
from arena_kit.cli import load_env, summary
from arena_kit.play import hosted, play_waves

from .agent import AGENTS, agent_factory

LOGS = Path("logs/sessions")


def pull(client, set_):
    """Save every ended session of a set that has its trace to logs/sessions/<set>/, once."""
    out = LOGS / set_
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    saved = 0
    for s in client.sessions(set_):
        path = out / f"{s['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}_{s['session_id']}.json"
        if s["status"] != "ended" or path.exists():
            continue
        state = client.session(s["session_id"])
        if not (state.get("result") or {}).get("trace"):  # final: the trace comes after the final
            continue
        try:
            state["backoffice"] = client.backoffice(s["session_id"])
        except ArenaError:
            state["backoffice"] = None
        path.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        saved += 1
    print(f"{saved} new sessions in {out}")


def main(argv=None):

"""Which agent plays a case. Our strategy grows here; until then `buyer` is the kit's LLMAgent."""

from arena_kit.agents import LLMAgent, NaiveAgent, llm_from_env
from arena_kit.data import DataPackage

AGENTS = ("buyer", "naive")


def agent_factory(name, data=None, complete=None):
    """A function that returns a fresh agent per case. `data`: the unpacked data package;
    `complete(system, user) -> str`: the model (default: from .env via `llm_from_env`)."""
    if name == "naive":
        return NaiveAgent
    package = None
    if data:
        package = DataPackage(data)
        package.lookup("")  # build the ID index once, before parallel agents share it
    complete = complete or llm_from_env()
    return lambda: LLMAgent(complete, package)

from .agent import AGENTS, agent_factory

LOGS = Path("logs/sessions")


def pull(client, set_):
    """Save every ended session of a set that has its trace to logs/sessions/<set>/, once."""
    out = LOGS / set_
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    saved = 0
    for s in client.sessions(set_):
        path = out / f"{s['case_id'].split(':')[-1]}_{s['session_id']}.json"
        if s["status"] != "ended" or path.exists():

        state = client.session(s["session_id"])

        except ArenaError:

content.text:
You don't need to spend practice tries to see real examples. The free part has already shown us the main thing the agent needs to get right.

## What we have to build

We write one function the kit calls on every turn: `decide(case, threads)`. It returns either an e-mail with up to 3 term sheets, an accept, or a walk away. The kit's runner does all the API work around it. Today `buyer/agent.py` just uses the kit's `LLMAgent`. That agent only reads the documents the case file points to, and it falls back to the kit's simple baseline agent whenever the model call fails.

## Endpoints (the kit's `ArenaClient` and `play` loop call these for us)

| Call | What for | Quota cost |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/cases?set=sandbox\|practice\|final` | full case files (need, rates, must-haves, alternative) | free |
| `POST /v1/sessions` | open a case; every supplier sends its quote e-mail and quote PDF | 1 try, practice only |
| `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{sup}/messages` | our e-mail and term sheets → supplier reply; also used to accept or walk away | none |
| `GET …/attachments/{id}` | quote PDF, cost breakdown, 8D report, delivery schedule | none |
| `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` and `…/backoffice` | after the case: score, cost breakdown, supplier's reasons, its internal discussion | none |
| `GET /v1/me` | quota left | none |

The agent may never call the event feed, the screen, the leaderboard or the results.

## How the score works

Per case: `(C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)`. C is the total euro cost over the whole case horizon, not the unit price, and `arena_kit.total_cost` computes it exactly. So the big wins are:

1. **Cover the full need.** Need that the deal doesn't cover is charged at the expensive fallback price plus a risk surcharge. In our only real run (sandbox D01, scored 0.20), the baseline agent bargained the price from 52.90 to 50.90 but signed 12 months on a 2-year need. That left €231k of the €441k cost as uncovered need. Extending the contract to 24 months alone would have been worth far more than the price talk.
2. **Trade terms, not just price.** Payment days, contract length, start date of the new price, volume and index clauses all carry euro weight. We can score every candidate term sheet offline before sending it.
3. **Never break a must-have** (that scores 0), and never accept a deal worse than our alternative.
4. **In `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases, don't squeeze too hard.** Pushing a supplier below a sustainable margin costs us. Brandlhuber and Nordmark already sell below their estimated cost.
5. **Read the supplier and pick the right argument.** That is where the data report comes in: a cash-short supplier trades price for faster payment, a hedged one ignores index arguments, and so on.

## Examples we already have, for free

- **All 21 case files** (sandbox D01 and D02, practice P01 to P19). I just saved them to `logs/cases/`; reading them used no quota. We can run `total_cost` on any term sheet offline, but C_best stays hidden until we play.
- **One sandbox session with full trace** in `logs/sessions/sandbox/D01_…json`.
- **Sandbox** (D01, D02): real supplier bots, unlimited, no leaderboard. This is where we iterate.
- **`arena-sim`**: local, but its supplier is scripted. Good for checking that the plumbing works, not for learning tactics.
- **Practice tries:** only 10 cases are hosted (P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18), and they count toward the practice leaderboard. We have 200 tries left and have used none. Each one should test a specific change.

## What the agent needs to do

1. **Before the case:** load the case file, the trigger letter, the supplier's signals and should-cost, and the index moves. This can't happen after a reply arrives, because we have 60 seconds per message.
2. **Each turn:**
   - Code builds candidate term sheets and ranks them by C, checking must-haves and the alternative.
   - The model writes the e-mail, with at most 3 cited facts, each with its correct figure.
   - The model call has a hard timeout well under 60 seconds.
3. **Read the reply:** status (`final_offer`, `agreed` and so on), standing offer, fields it left out (those close on its standard terms from the quote PDF), claim results and attachments.
4. **Close well:** accept when the gap is small or the supplier says `final_offer`, walk away when the alternative is cheaper, and handle RFQs with 2 to 3 suppliers in parallel.
5. **Final:** run all of a wave's cases in parallel within 8 minutes, with no human in the loop. The kit's `buyer run --set final` already handles this.

## Blocker

`.env` holds only the arena variables and no LLM settings (`LLM_PROVIDER`, `LLM_MODEL`, API key). As configured, `uv run buyer play` will crash on startup until those are added.

## Proposed first step

Build a cost optimiser in code: for each case, search the negotiable options with `total_cost` and set the target and the walk-away line. Then iterate on D01 and D02 in the sandbox and spend practice tries only to confirm improvements.

import json
cases = {c['case_id']: c for s in ('sandbox','practice') for c in json.load(open(f'logs/cases/{s}.json'))}
for cid, c in cases.items():
    b, fx, opt, neg = c['buyer'], c.get('fixed_terms', {}), c.get('term_options', {}), c['negotiable']
    need_months = round(12 * b['horizon_years'])
    m = fx.get('contract_months'); v = fx.get('volume_per_year')
    m_src = 'fixed' if m is not None else ('negotiable ' + str(opt.get('contract_months')) if 'contract_months' in neg else 'supplier standard')
    v_src = 'fixed' if v is not None else ('negotiable ' + str(opt.get('volume_per_year', 'free')) if 'volume_per_year' in neg else 'supplier standard')
    print(f"{cid[5:]:4} need {b['need_per_year']}/yr x {need_months} mo | contract {m if m is not None else '':>3} {m_src:28} | volume {v if v is not None else '':>6} {v_src:24} | eff.date {'neg '+str(opt.get('effective_date')) if 'effective_date' in neg else fx.get('effective_date','-')}")
EOF

content.text:
Our cost C is fully defined by the case file. So most items on your list are either given or simple arithmetic. What we actually have to model is the supplier's hidden side: its cost, what cash is worth to it, its capacity, its real quality, and how it concedes. **C_best is not an input. It is what those supplier models plus a term search produce.** Every finished practice or sandbox case reveals the true C_best, so we can calibrate against it.

## 1. Your list, sorted

| Item | What we have | Do we need a model? |
|---|---|---|
| **Interest** | Given: 8 % a year, reference 60 days, the same in all 21 cases | Ours, no. The supplier's, yes (model B) |
| **Demand forecast** | The need (`need_per_year` × `horizon_years`) is fixed per case | No. The forecast is useful as a citable argument (part 310010 is forecast +10.1 %) and as a guard: committed volume above the need is paid for anyway |
| **Covered or not** | Arithmetic: `min(volume, need) × min(months/12, horizon)`. The rest costs the fallback price plus a risk surcharge | No, just a rule. In 14 of 21 cases contract length or volume is our choice or left to the supplier's standard terms |
| **Lead time** | Our side is given: the lead time we need, € per day late, must-haves | The supplier's capability, yes (model C) |
| **Product quality** | Our side is given: € per defect. C charges committed ppm minus chargebacks | The supplier's real ppm, yes (model D) |
| **Relationship** | Rates given in `stabilise` and `secure_supply` cases: the margin a healthy supplier needs, and € per margin point it falls short | The supplier's margin needs models A and B |
| **EU market data** | 33 series (Eurostat producer prices, labour cost, World Bank metals, ECB exchange rates, German power prices), ending 2026-06 to 2026-09. The case gives the expected index path for C | No forecasting. We use it for arguments and to check how much of a price increase is justified |
| **Supplier scoring** | Already built (`analysis/out/profiles.csv`): scorecard, how late we pay, finances, signals from notes | It feeds models B to E |
| **C_best** | Revealed exactly after each practice or sandbox case | It is the output of the term search over models A to E |

## 2. What arrives during a session

- **Quote PDF with the supplier's standard terms.** Every field we leave out closes on them. The kit already parses it.
- **Each reply:** the supplier's current offer, its status (`final_offer`, `agreed`), fields it left out, whether our data claims checked out, reply delay, and how long the offer stays valid.
- **On request:**
  - a cost breakdown XLSX, with the supplier's own cost elements, if it is open enough to send one;
  - an 8D quality report with a ppm commitment;
  - a delivery schedule.
- **After the case (practice and sandbox only):**
  - the exact `c_open` and `c_best`;
  - our cost breakdown, including the relationship charge calculated from the supplier's true numbers;
  - the supplier's reasons for each move;
  - its internal back-office discussion.

## 3. What's hidden, and the models for it

| Model | Estimates | Needed for | Data we have | How we calibrate it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Supplier cost** | Its full cost per unit and its floor | Relationship charge, C_best, our target price | Plant-level cost estimates (±5 %) for P01, P02, P03, P09, P10, P14, P17; generic German-cost estimates for the RFQs P05 and P06; nothing for the other 10. Plus index updates since each estimate, country cost factors, and price history. 5 suppliers once sold below full cost to keep volume | The relationship charge in a result gives the true margin, and from that the true cost |
| **B. What cash is worth to the supplier** | Its interest rate | How much price it gives for faster payment; its margin | Cash discounts offered by 4 suppliers (implying 37 to 56 % a year), cash-need notes, "payment within 10 days" quote remarks, credit ratings worsening (Wälzhammer, Weißacher), equity ratio, distress news | Watch how its price moves across payment-day options in the sandbox |
| **C. Capacity and lead time** | What more volume, a longer contract or faster delivery costs or earns it | Capacity cases P09, P10; RFQs with lead-time must-haves | Spare or full capacity in notes and news, our share of its turnover, 5,400 order lines with requested, confirmed and delivered dates | Delivery schedule XLSX |
| **D. Real quality** | The ppm it really achieves | Quality cases P11, P12; any case with a defect cost | 9 quarters of scorecards, 1,033 complaints with ppm | 8D report |
| **E. How it concedes** | How far and how fast it moves, and when it walks | Pacing over 10 messages, when to accept | 300 past price negotiations (asked vs settled), notes that moves above 2 % need approval, supplier signals from notes | Supplier reasons in practice replays |

**How the C_best estimate works:** for each supplier, take the cheapest combination of allowed terms that keeps the deal above that supplier's floor; then take the cheaper of that and our alternative. In `stabilise` cases the best deal sits a little below the healthy margin, because the charge for the first margin points is small.

## 4. Inputs you didn't list

- **Contract notice position.** P01's letter gives 51 days' notice; the contract requires 90 days and fixes prices per calendar year. The arena checks this claim (letter ID plus contract ID). It justifies a later start date for the new price, and units bought before that date are at the old price.
- **The alternative and competing quotes.** The cost of our alternative can already be computed for every case. In RFQs we can cite a rival's offer, but citing it reveals it to the other supplier.
- **Must-haves.** Breaking one scores 0.
- **Index clause design.** Series, material share, deadband and base month matter in P02, P08, P14, P16 and P18, plus when the supplier's material hedge runs out.
- **Exchange rates** for suppliers in CZ, PL, HU, TR and CN. ECB rates are citable index IDs.
- **Tooling** in P06.
- **Our own record.** How late we pay a supplier, and how much of its turnover we are.
- **Claim rules.** Exact values from `facts.json`, ±0.5 point tolerance, at most 3 claims per message, each ID once per case.
- **Sunday release** and the case-specific facts in hidden cases, read at runtime.
- **The 60-second limit.** Everything above has to be computed when the session opens.

## 5. Why this matters: our one real result

In sandbox case D01 the kit's baseline agent scored **0.20**. At the same price of 50.90, a 24-month contract instead of 12 and an April start for the new price would have scored **0.81**, with no extra price concession. Working back from the revealed C_best, the best possible price was between 49.55 (30 days, December start) and 50.13 (60 days, April start), assuming no relationship charge at the best deal.

## 6. Build order

1. **Term search (no model needed).** Try every allowed term combination, score each with `total_cost` and the standard terms, and check must-haves and the alternative. This alone fixes losses like D01.
2. **Models A and B**, which give the relationship charge and the C_best estimate.
3. **Claim generator** built from `facts.json`.
4. **Pacing policy** (model E). Models C and D only for capacity and quality cases.

**Decision for you:** playing each of the 10 hosted cases once with step 1 costs 10 of the team's 200 tries. It gives us 10 exact C_best values and relationship charges to calibrate models A and B. D01 and D02 in the sandbox are free to run as often as we like. Should we spend those 10?

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Rules for AI coding agents working in this repo. Humans follow them too.
4	
5	- Hackathon repo (EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026). Code freeze and Live Final
6	  Sunday 12:00. Working agent first, polish second.
7	- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding
8	  compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.
9	- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement.
10	  No speculative abstractions, configuration, or indirection.
11	- Grow the system in layers: smallest version that works end to end, then add on
12	  top of a product that already works. Never trade a working product for
13	  unfinished complexity.
14	- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
15	- Prefer established libraries already in the project before adding new ones or
16	  writing your own implementation. Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper:
17	  the cost function, quote parsing, data lookup and the runners already exist.
18	- Never commit secrets. Keys go into `.env` (gitignored). Never print, log or paste the
19	  arena key anywhere (code, logs, issues, Discord, PR text).
20	- All changes go through a pull request against `main`, reviewed by one teammate.
21	  Branch naming: `<firstname>/<topic>`. Agents may commit, push their branch and open the PR
22	  (`gh pr create`) on their own; they never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
23	- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
24	- Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines or fewer.
25	
26	## Challenge: Tacto Negotiation Arena
27	
28	We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker. Our agent
29	negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes
30	one term sheet per case, or walks away. Full text: `docs/challenge.md` (brief), `docs/api.md`
31	(API, claim checks, cost formula), `docs/submission.md`. Upstream:
32	https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit, FAQ: https://arena.tacto.ai/faq.
33	
34	**Score.** Per case `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is the total
35	cost in euros over the case horizon: price, uncovered need, payment terms, freight, lead time,
36	quality, tooling, index clause, and in `stabilise` / `secure_supply` cases a charge for leaving
37	the supplier below a sustainable margin. Not price. `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C exactly.
38	No deal scores the alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
39	
40	**Live Final.** Sunday 12:00, five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, all cases of a wave in
41	parallel. New suppliers; up to a third combine supplier and case types practice never shows.
42	Some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release. Wave score = mean case score x 100; total = sum.
43	
44	**Hard rules (breaking one can disqualify us):**
45	- No human in the loop during the final. The runner is started before 12:00 and left alone.
46	- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
47	  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`. Those are for people.
48	- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams.
49	- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.
50	
51	**Hard limits:**
52	- 60 seconds per message per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A late message is a
53	  timeout; three in a row end the thread. Heavy work happens before a session is opened.
54	- 10 messages per thread (case `round_limit`), up to 3 term sheets per message, every term sheet
55	  carries every `negotiable` field.
56	- Max 3 claim checks per message; one argument per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence.
57	  An unknown ID or wrong figure is `contradicted` and costs trust.
58	- 10 calls per second and 10 open sessions per key.
59	- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team, shared across all
60	  machines.** Sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.
61	
62	## Repo map
63	
64	| Path | What |
65	|---|---|
66	| `buyer/agent.py` | which agent plays a case; our strategy grows here (today: the kit's `LLMAgent`) |
67	| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
68	| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
69	| `docs/` | brief, API, submission guide (copied from upstream) |
70	| `data/package/` | the data package, gitignored; `uv run arena data` fetches it (Sunday also `data/release-sunday/`) |
71	| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office, gitignored; `uv run buyer pull` fetches them |
72	
73	`arena_kit` (Tacto's starter kit) is a git dependency pinned in `pyproject.toml`. We do not patch
74	it; we wrap it. Its README is the best guide to its modules:
75	https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
76	
77	## Commands
78	
79	```sh
80	uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
81	uv run arena data                               # data package into data/ (again Sunday after 08:00)
82	uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
83	uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .         # before every PR
84	uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free, real supplier bots
85	uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
86	uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all 10 hosted practice cases: costs 10
87	uv run buyer pull --set practice                # every finished session -> logs/sessions/
88	uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10      # the Live Final, Sunday before 12:00
89	uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API with a scripted supplier
90	```
91	
92	`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours. The MCP server `arena-data`
93	(`.mcp.json`) gives coding agents SQL, ID lookup and documents over the data package.
94	
95	## Working on the negotiation agent
96	
97	- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (term sheets, accept,
98	  walk away) is computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`. Every figure
99	  in an e-mail comes from code, next to its data ID. The model reads the supplier and writes.
100	- **Never accept** a term sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative.
101	  Price unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF (`docs.standard_terms`).
102	- **Generalise, don't memorise.** No logic keyed on practice case IDs or supplier IDs. Knowledge
103	  derived from the data package at runtime is fine; it must also work for unseen suppliers.
104	- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data: call notes, letters, news, quote
105	  remarks, payment history, scorecards. Trade what is cheap for us (payment days, contract
106	  length, volume, dates) for what it values.
107	- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
108	- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
109	  fails. Measure latency per move.
110	
111	## The learning loop
112	
113	1. Try on the simulator or the sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect
114	   to help, and check `uv run arena me` before batch runs: teammates share the 200.
115	2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, then read `logs/sessions/`. The trace holds the supplier's
116	   reasons for every move, the back office its internal discussion, the result the cost breakdown.
117	3. Find why C_deal missed C_best (which lever, which argument, which timing), change the agent,
118	   score candidate term sheets offline with `total_cost`, then play again.
119	4. Write what you learned about supplier behaviour into the PR description, so the team and
120	   the pitch can use it.
121	
122	## Sunday
123	
124	- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
125	- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
126	- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
127	- Before 12:00: start `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`
128	  from `main`, submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.
129

- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines or fewer.

## Challenge: Tacto Negotiation Arena

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker. Our agent
negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes
one term sheet per case, or walks away. Full text: `docs/challenge.md` (brief), `docs/api.md`
(API, claim checks, cost formula), `docs/submission.md`. Upstream:
https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit, FAQ: https://arena.tacto.ai/faq.

**Score.** Per case `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is the total
cost in euros over the case horizon: price, uncovered need, payment terms, freight, lead time,
quality, tooling, index clause, and in `stabilise` / `secure_supply` cases a charge for leaving
the supplier below a sustainable margin. Not price. `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C exactly.
No deal scores the alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.

**Live Final.** Sunday 12:00, five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, all cases of a wave in
parallel. New suppliers; up to a third combine supplier and case types practice never shows.
Some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release. Wave score = mean case score x 100; total = sum.

**Hard rules (breaking one can disqualify us):**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner is started before 12:00 and left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`. Those are for people.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams.
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 seconds per message per thread, counted from the supplier's reply. A late message is a
  timeout; three in a row end the thread. Heavy work happens before a session is opened.
- 10 messages per thread (case `round_limit`), up to 3 term sheets per message, every term sheet
  carries every `negotiable` field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message; one argument per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence.
  An unknown ID or wrong figure is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls per second and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team, shared across all
  machines.** Sandbox (`case:D01`, `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Repo map

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `buyer/agent.py` | which agent plays a case; our strategy grows here (today: the kit's `LLMAgent`) |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `docs/` | brief, API, submission guide (copied from upstream) |
| `data/package/` | the data package, gitignored; `uv run arena data` fetches it (Sunday also `data/release-sunday/`) |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office, gitignored; `uv run buyer pull` fetches them |

`arena_kit` (Tacto's starter kit) is a git dependency pinned in `pyproject.toml`. We do not patch
it; we wrap it. Its README is the best guide to its modules:
https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/ (again Sunday after 08:00)
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .         # before every PR
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free, real supplier bots
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all 10 hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # every finished session -> logs/sessions/
uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10      # the Live Final, Sunday before 12:00
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API with a scripted supplier
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours. The MCP server `arena-data`
(`.mcp.json`) gives coding agents SQL, ID lookup and documents over the data package.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (term sheets, accept,
  walk away) is computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`. Every figure
  in an e-mail comes from code, next to its data ID. The model reads the supplier and writes.
- **Never accept** a term sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative.
  Price unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF (`docs.standard_terms`).
- **Generalise, don't memorise.** No logic keyed on practice case IDs or supplier IDs. Knowledge
  derived from the data package at runtime is fine; it must also work for unseen suppliers.
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data: call notes, letters, news, quote
  remarks, payment history, scorecards. Trade what is cheap for us (payment days, contract
  length, volume, dates) for what it values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or the sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect
   to help, and check `uv run arena me` before batch runs: teammates share the 200.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, then read `logs/sessions/`. The trace holds the supplier's
   reasons for every move, the back office its internal discussion, the result the cost breakdown.
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best (which lever, which argument, which timing), change the agent,
   score candidate term sheets offline with `total_cost`, then play again.
4. Write what you learned about supplier behaviour into the PR description, so the team and
   the pitch can use it.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00: start `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`
  from `main`, submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

# Learnings

Running list of what we found out about the arena, the suppliers and the data. Newest entry on
top of each section. How to add entries: `AGENTS.md`, "The learning loop".

Tags: `arena` seen in a session (cite session or case), `data` from the data package (cite table
or ID), `rules` follows from `docs/api.md` or the kit's code. Untested ideas go under Hypotheses
until a session confirms or kills them.

## Score and terms

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Coverage beats price.** D01 (sandbox, kit's naive agent) scored 0.20. It
  talked the price from 52.90 to 50.90 but signed 12 months on a 24-month need, so EUR 231k of the
  EUR 441k C was uncovered need plus its risk. The same 50.90 with 24 months and a 2027-04-01 start
  scores 0.81 (relationship charge left out). Evidence: `logs/sessions/sandbox/D01_b3db88eb8e8423b7.json`.
  → Choose contract length and volume to cover need x horizon before haggling.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01 revealed C_best 408,623.99 (C_open 448,810.67). Backed out with
  `total_cost`: the best package implies a price of 49.55 (30 days, December start) to 50.13
  (60 days, April start), 1.5 to 2.7 % below the 50.90 we got, assuming no relationship charge
  at the optimum.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01's deal at 50.90 carried no relationship charge, so the foundry's margin
  there was at least the sustainable 4 %: its full cost is at most about 48.9, close to the
  current price 48.60. One result already bounds a supplier's cost.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` Results in practice and sandbox reveal exact `c_best` and our cost breakdown,
  relationship charge included, computed with the supplier's true numbers. A non-zero charge gives
  its true margin and so its true full cost: our calibration channel for the cost model.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` The relationship charge (`stabilise`, `secure_supply`) grows with the square
  of the first 5 missing margin points, so the cheapest deal sits below the sustainable margin
  (D01: about 2 points below its 4 %), unless the supplier's cost floor binds first.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` In 14 of 21 case files contract length or volume is ours to pick or left to
  the supplier's standard terms: D01, D02, P03, P04, P07, P08, P09, P10, P14 to P19.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` Units bought before `effective_date` cost the current price, so a later start
  is worth months x volume x price step. Negotiable in D01, P01, P13.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` Our money: 8 % a year, reference 60 days, in all 21 cases. Paying 30 days
  earlier costs 0.67 % of spend.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` No alternative, so walking away scores 0: D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17.

## Supplier behaviour

- 2026-10-10 `arena` D01's foundry answered four content-free "we need a better price" e-mails
  with shrinking steps: 52.90, 51.90, 51.40, 51.10, 50.90 (-1.00, -0.50, -0.30, -0.20). It kept
  payment days, contract length and start date exactly as in our sheets; it did not offer better
  terms unprompted. Its reasons: "our calculation stays internal".
- 2026-10-10 `arena` Suppliers argue with data too: D01's opening e-mail cited WAGES-METAL +3.1 %
  as 28 % of its cost (a typed `index_change` claim in the opening move).
- 2026-10-10 `data` Price letters overshoot the index-weighted cost move of the part's drivers:
  P01 +9.5 % vs +2.3 %, P13 +7.0 % vs +4.0 %, P17 +8.0 % vs +5.5 %. P02 +6.5 % vs +6.6 % is fair.
- 2026-10-10 `data` Some incumbents sell below should-cost today (error about 5 %): P17 -8.4 %,
  P02 -7.6 %, P01 -4.8 %. All `stabilise`: pushing them lower adds relationship charge.
- 2026-10-10 `data` 225 past renewals asked +1.4 % on average and settled -1.1 %. Median settled
  0.0 %; 82 % ended flat or lower (`negotiation_history`).
- 2026-10-10 `data` Second-source quotes are 8 to 21 % above the incumbent. Exceptions: DN 65
  flange +1.9 % (sup:70240), coupling hub +9.6 %. A switch threat is a bluff in most cases.
- 2026-10-10 `data` We pay late: Saalach 19 days, Wälzhammer 16, Lindlbauer 13 on average.
  Seven suppliers sent an overdue-invoice letter (`invoices`; documents ending `-P`).
- 2026-10-10 `data` Cash discounts in the vendor master show what cash is worth to 4 suppliers:
  2 to 3 % for 16 to 20 days earlier is 37 to 56 % a year (sup:70210, 70230, 70280, 70350).
- 2026-10-10 `data` Persona traits are written in one or two fixed phrases each, across call
  notes, meeting notes, quote remarks and news: 12 traits, regex `SIGNALS` and levers `LEVER` in
  `analysis/explore.py`. Holiday, ISO, contact-person, packaging and trade-fair mails are noise.

## Arguments and claims

- 2026-10-10 `data` P01's letter gives 51 days' notice (`doc:20260911-70110-P01`); the contract
  requires 90 and fixes prices per calendar year (`ctr:4600070110`, clause `#3.1`). The arena
  checks letter against contract notice days. Supports a 2027 start.
- 2026-10-10 `data` Citable market counters: industrial power -43 % on 2022 (`news:20260912-30`),
  iron castings +1.8 % year on year (`news:20260914-31`).
- 2026-10-10 `data` Forecast changes are citable as volume arguments: `fc:310010@2026-09` +10.1 %.
- 2026-10-10 `data` Case alternatives are `quote:72000xx` in `facts.json`, but the case file's
  alternative terms rule C_alt and can differ (P01: lead time 70 in the case, 56 in the quote;
  plus tooling 1,500 and 2,376 ppm).

## Data and tooling

- 2026-10-10 `data` Case files of all 21 cases come free from `GET /v1/cases` (no session, no
  quota), saved in `logs/cases/{sandbox,practice}.json`. Hosted for practice: P01, P02, P03, P04,
  P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18.
- 2026-10-10 `data` Own-plant should-cost (about 5 % error) exists for P01, P02, P03, P09, P10,
  P14, P17, exactly the `stabilise` / `secure_supply` cases that need it. German-base estimates
  for the new-part RFQs P05, P06. Nothing for the other 10.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` The kit's `llm_from_env` reads `LLM_MODEL` (plus provider settings);
  without it, `buyer play` with our default agent fails before the first move.
- 2026-10-10 `data` pandas is not a project dependency; the exploration runs with
  `uv run --no-project --with pandas python analysis/explore.py`.

## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)

- Cash-short suppliers (cash-need notes, cash discount, credit downgrade) give more price for 14
  to 30 days payment than the 0.67 % per 30 days it costs us.
- Stale-costing suppliers concede after a verified index claim; hedged suppliers answer index
  claims with "not our reality" until the hedge ends.
- Price-frozen suppliers move on payment days, logistics and contract length only.
- Suppliers with "approval above 2 %" notes move at most 2 % per round.
- The cost floor is full cost; the five that once sold below full cost to keep volume
  (sup:70110, 70120, 70130, 70160, 70550) may go lower.

# Overview

What the agent has to do, what it needs to know, where each piece comes from and which parts
need a model. Findings go to `learnings.md`; API details are in `docs/api.md`.
State: 2026-10-10.

## The job

The kit calls our agent's `decide(case, threads)` once per turn (`arena_kit.play`). It returns an
e-mail with up to 3 term sheets, an accept, or a walk away. The kit handles sessions,
attachments, timeouts and the final's waves. Per case: prepare before the first move (60 s per
move), negotiate up to 10 messages per thread, close.

Score per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1.

| Endpoint | Use | Quota |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/cases?set=sandbox\|practice\|final` | case files | free |
| `POST /v1/sessions` | open a case: every supplier's quote e-mail and quote PDF | practice: 1 of 200 |
| `POST /v1/sessions/{sid}/threads/{supplier}/messages` | our e-mail, its reply; also accept or walk away | none |
| `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}/attachments/{id}` | quote PDF, cost breakdown XLSX, 8D report, delivery schedule | none |
| `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}`, `.../backoffice` | after the end: score, c_best, breakdown, reasons, back office | none |
| `GET /v1/me` | quota left | none |

Agent code never calls the event feed, screen, leaderboard or results.

## Inputs

### Given by the case file: no model
Need per year and horizon, current and fallback price, fallback risk, interest rate (8 %) and
reference payment days (60), lead time we need and EUR per day late, EUR per defect, category
goal, index risk and the expected index path, sustainable margin and EUR per margin point
(`stabilise`, `secure_supply`), freight per Incoterm, must-haves, the alternative with its terms,
negotiable fields, fixed terms, allowed options, round limit, refs, case-only facts.

Arithmetic, not models: coverage `min(V, N) x min(M/12, H)`, early-payment interest, freight,
late days, quality cost, index clause cost, C of the alternative (`arena_kit.total_cost`).

### Arrives in the session
- Round 0 quote PDF with the supplier's standard terms. Every field we leave out closes on them
  (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- Each reply: standing offer, status (`open`, `final_offer`, `agreed`, `walked_away`, `no_bid`),
  missing fields, claim results, reply delay, validity.
- On request: cost breakdown XLSX (an open supplier's own cost elements), 8D report (ppm
  commitment), delivery schedule (capacity, lead time).

### Revealed after a practice or sandbox case
Exact `c_open`, `c_best`, `c_deal`, our cost breakdown including the relationship charge computed
with the supplier's true numbers, the supplier's reasons per move, the back office.

### Hidden: the supplier models

| Model | Estimates | Needed for | Data | Calibrate with |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Supplier cost | full cost per unit, its floor | relationship charge, C_best, target price | `should_cost` (own plant for P01, P02, P03, P09, P10, P14, P17; German base for P05, P06), cost drivers x index moves since the estimate, country factors (`company.md`), `price_conditions`, `negotiation_history` | relationship charge in results gives the true margin |
| B. Cash value to the supplier | its interest rate (`supplier_value`) | price for faster payment; its margin | cash discounts in `suppliers`, cash-need notes, quote remarks, `supplier_intel` credit index and equity ratio, distress news | price moves across payment-day options in the sandbox |
| C. Capacity and lead time | what volume, contract length, faster delivery cost or earn it | capacity cases, RFQs, lead-time must-haves | capacity notes and news, our spend vs its turnover, `po_lines` + `goods_receipts` (requested, confirmed, received) | delivery schedule XLSX |
| D. Real quality | the ppm it really achieves | quality cases, any case with a defect cost | `scorecards` (9 quarters), `quality_notifications` (1,033) | 8D report |
| E. Concession behaviour | how far and fast it moves, when it walks | pacing over 10 messages, when to accept | `negotiation_history` (300 events), approval notes, persona signals | practice traces |

C_best estimate: per supplier, the cheapest combination of allowed terms whose value to the
supplier (`arena_kit.cost.supplier_value`) stays above its floor; then the cheaper of that and
the alternative. In `stabilise` cases the optimum leaves the supplier somewhat below the
sustainable margin, because the first missing points cost little.

### Also needed
- Contract notice position: letter notice days against the contract's (`doc` + `ctr` claim),
  calendar-year price clauses. Drives `effective_date`.
- Index clause design for P02, P08, P14, P16, P18: series, material share, deadband, base month;
  existing clauses in `contract_clauses`; hedge end dates from notes and quote remarks.
- Exchange rates for suppliers in CZ, PL, HU, TR, CN: ECB series are citable `idx` IDs.
- Tooling (P06). Rival offers in RFQs (citable as `offer:` IDs, which reveals them).
- Claim mechanics: exact values in `facts.json`, ±0.5 pp, at most 3 per message, each ID once
  per case.
- Sunday release (`data/release-sunday/`) and the case's own `facts`: read at runtime.

## Build order

1. Term search, no model: every combination of allowed options, scored with `total_cost` and the
   standard terms, guarded by must-haves and C_alt. Fixes D01-type losses.
2. Models A and B: relationship charge and the C_best estimate, i.e. target and walk-away line.
3. Claim generator from `facts.json` and the index tables.
4. Pacing policy (model E). Models C and D only for capacity and quality cases.

Open decision: spend 10 of the team's 200 practice sessions to play each hosted case once and
harvest exact C_best values for calibration.

## Data package map

| Table | Use |
|---|---|
| `suppliers`, `supplier_intel` | profile, country, cash discount, credit index, equity ratio |
| `parts`, `sourcing` | price unit, ABC class, approved second sources |
| `price_conditions`, `negotiation_history` | price path; how past asks settled |
| `contracts`, `contract_clauses` | notice days, price basis, existing index clauses |
| `po_lines`, `goods_receipts` | real lead times, on-time delivery, order prices (`po` claims) |
| `invoices` | how late we pay |
| `scorecards`, `quality_notifications` | OTD, ppm, open 8D (`sc`, `qn` claims) |
| `forecasts`, `forecast_lines` | volume changes (`fc` claims) |
| `rfqs`, `quotes` | rival prices, past terms, remarks (signals) |
| `spend_cube` | our spend per supplier, long tail |
| `index_series`, `index_values`, `cost_drivers` | justified increase, `idx` claims, index clauses |
| `should_cost` | full-cost estimate (`cost` claims) |
| `news`, `documents` + `correspondence/` | persona signals, trigger letters |
| `facts.json` | exact values the arena checks |

Exploration: `uv run --no-project --with pandas python analysis/explore.py` writes
`analysis/out/` (profiles, fairness, triggers, notes CSVs and `report.html`). Published report
(private): https://claude.ai/artifact/Dz619qxLsZgJNgiUe2MycU

## Practice cases

Ask: the letter's increase. Index move: cost-driver-weighted index change since the current
price. Margin now: (price - should-cost) / price. Signals: those of the trigger document's
supplier.

| Case | Hosted | Type | Goal | Supplier(s) | Ask | Index move | Margin now | Alternative | Signals |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P01 | yes | price_increase | stabilise | 70110 | +9.5 % | +2.3 % | -4.8 % | quote | cash_need, partnership_2022, stale_costing |
| P02 | yes | price_increase | stabilise | 70510 | +6.5 % | +6.6 % | -7.6 % | quote | approval_2pct |
| P03 | yes | renewal | stabilise | 70530 |  | +6.1 % | +2.3 % | quote | approval_2pct, price_frozen |
| P04 | yes | renewal | routine | 70620 |  | +0.6 % |  | quote | deprioritising_us, open_book, price_frozen |
| P05 | yes | rfq | leverage | 70210, 70240, 70250 |  |  |  | none | complains_late_pay, reference_customer, spare_capacity, stale_costing |
| P06 |  | rfq | stabilise | 70120, 70150 |  |  |  | none | partnership_2022 |
| P07 | yes | bundling | routine | 70610 |  | +1.1 % |  | current_contract | approval_2pct, spare_capacity |
| P08 | yes | raw_material | leverage | 70710 |  | -3.2 % |  | quote | hedged, open_book |
| P09 |  | capacity | secure_supply | 70220 |  | +4.1 % | +3.9 % | quote | capacity_full, cash_need, reference_customer |
| P10 | yes | capacity | secure_supply | 70410 |  | +0.9 % | +18.7 % | none | approval_2pct, capacity_full |
| P11 | yes | quality | quality_first | 70140 |  | +2.3 % |  | quote | cash_need |
| P12 |  | quality | quality_first | 70310 |  | +2.7 % |  | current_contract | cash_need |
| P13 |  | price_increase | leverage | 70230 | +7.0 % | +4.0 % |  | quote | cash_need, complains_late_pay, open_book, stale_costing |
| P14 |  | renewal | stabilise | 70560 |  | +3.8 % | +3.7 % | none | approval_2pct, hedged |
| P15 |  | bundling | routine | 70430 |  | +2.0 % |  | current_contract | deprioritising_us, open_book |
| P16 |  | raw_material | leverage | 70720 |  | +6.7 % |  | quote | open_book, reference_customer |
| P17 |  | price_increase | stabilise | 70550 | +8.0 % | +5.5 % | -8.4 % | none | approval_2pct |
| P18 | yes | raw_material | leverage | 70740 |  | -3.2 % |  | quote | approval_2pct, deprioritising_us, open_book |
| P19 |  | renewal | routine | 70640 |  | +0.6 % |  | quote | approval_2pct, deprioritising_us, spare_capacity |

## Supplier signals and levers

Levers are hypotheses until a session confirms them (`learnings.md`).

| Signal | Lever |
|---|---|
| cash_need | pay faster (14 to 30 days) for price; it values cash over list price |
| spare_capacity | offer volume or extra parts; idle capacity makes a lower price cheap for it |
| capacity_full | trade a firm 12 to 24 month commitment for price and allocation |
| open_book | ask for the cost breakdown XLSX, argue line by line against should-cost |
| stale_costing | index data disarms it: show the real index path since its last price |
| partnership_2022 | acknowledge 2022, frame the deal as partnership, avoid hard threats |
| reference_customer | it values the reference: tone and long-term framing move it |
| approval_2pct | keep each move at 2 % or less, or give its committee time |
| deprioritising_us | weak leverage: bundle volume, or use the alternative |
| price_frozen | price will not move: trade payment days, logistics, call-off flexibility |
| hedged | index arguments are "not our reality" until its hedge ends |
| complains_late_pay | our late payment hurt trust: promise and keep payment terms |

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents working in this repo. Humans follow them too.

- Hackathon repo (EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026). Code freeze and Live Final
  Sunday 12:00. Working agent first, polish second.
- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding
  compatibility layers, fallbacks, or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement.
  No speculative abstractions, configuration, or indirection.
- Grow the system in layers: smallest version that works end to end, then add on
  top of a product that already works. Never trade a working product for
  unfinished complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Prefer established libraries already in the project before adding new ones or
  writing your own implementation. Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper:
  the cost function, quote parsing, data lookup and the runners already exist.
- Never commit secrets. Keys go into `.env` (gitignored). Never print, log or paste the
  arena key anywhere (code, logs, issues, Discord, PR text).
- All changes go through a pull request against `main`, reviewed by one teammate.
  Branch naming: `<firstname>/<topic>`. Agents may commit, push their branch and open the PR
  (`gh pr create`) on their own; they never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- No em-dashes in prose or user-facing copy.
- Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines or fewer.

## Challenge: Tacto Negotiation Arena

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a fictional German pump maker. Our agent
negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes
one term sheet per case, or walks away. Full text: `docs/challenge.md` (brief), `docs/api.md`
(API, claim checks, cost formula), `docs/submission.md`. Upstream:
https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit, FAQ: https://arena.tacto.ai/faq.

I wrote the notes into a new gitignored `notes/` folder and added a rule to `AGENTS.md` so agents keep a growing list there:

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.
4	
5	Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
6	12:00. Working agent first, polish second.
7	
8	## Rules
9	
10	- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
11	  fallbacks or migrations.
12	- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
13	  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
14	- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
15	  complexity.
16	- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
17	- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
18	  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
19	  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
20	- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
21	- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
22	  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
23	- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
24	- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.
25	
26	## The challenge
27	
28	We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
29	supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.
30	
31	- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
32	  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
33	  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
34	  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
35	- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
36	  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
37	  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.
38	
39	**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
40	- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
41	- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
42	  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
43	- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
44	- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.
45	
46	**Hard limits:**
47	- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
48	- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
49	  field.
50	- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
51	  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
52	- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
53	- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
54	  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.
55	
56	## Where things are
57	
58	| Path | What |
59	|---|---|
60	| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
61	| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
62	| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
63	| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
64	| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
65	| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
66	| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
67	| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
68	| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
69	| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
70	| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
71	| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |
72	
73	The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.
74	
75	## Commands
76	
77	```sh
78	uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
79	uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
80	uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
81	uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
82	uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
83	uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
84	uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
85	uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
86	uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
87	```
88	
89	`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.
90	
91	## Working on the negotiation agent
92	
93	- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
94	  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
95	  comes from code next to its data ID.
96	- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
97	  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
98	- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
99	  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
100	- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
101	  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
102	- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
103	  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
104	- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
105	- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
106	  fails. Measure latency per move.
107	
108	## The learning loop
109	
110	1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
111	   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
112	2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
113	3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
114	4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
115	   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
116	   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
117	   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.
118	
119	## Sunday
120	
121	- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
122	- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
123	- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
124	- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
125	  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

   counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once

  12-month change - deadband)` of the price (Nordmark 8.5 %, Donautal and Werdenfels 0.4 to 2.7 %,
  which is exactly our cost of their clause, so no trade there); we pay `material_share x (path -
  deadband) + the index risk`. → `economics.clause_trade`: offer the clause with the largest net
  gain (ties: the widest deadband) from round 1 at the price worth the same to the supplier as
  our anchor, in relationship goals no lower than the relationship optimum (P02: 361.71 with the
  full cost capped at the quote less the sustainable margin). P14 (copper, stabilise) gains 21 %
  of the price by this rule, P16 (PPI-C241, leverage) 2 %.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **A falling cost driver over the best window moves the first counter (v10).**
  The claim bank only knew 12-month index changes, where the distributors' main driver AS-14404
  rose 5.9 %; over the window the arena checks (any two months up to 12 apart, ending within the
  last 12) it fell 5.5 % from 2026-06 to 2026-09 and PPI-C2431 2.3 % from June. Cited in round 1
  (`practice-v10.log`): Donautal's first counter 5.40 (5.43 to 5.60 in 14 runs before), then
  5.33, 5.28, 5.26 final, score 0.670; Werdenfels 5.30 (5.50 to 5.60 before), then 5.20, 5.10,
  final 5.10, score 0.621 (was 0.485). Both gave four counters instead of three. A second run
  repeated Werdenfels' path exactly (5.30, 5.20, 5.10) and Donautal's within noise (5.40, 5.35,
  5.31, 5.30); with the hedge letter moved out of round 1 Donautal opened at 5.52 (one run), so
  the letter stays first. Electricity (PPI-D351) fell 6.1 % from 2025-11 for P01, P05 and P11:
  Kalwisz still stopped at 45.50, P05 closed at 0.81 (best 0.828). → Every driver's largest fall
  within 12 months, ranked above order prices and forecasts.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **v8 and v9 on practice (12 runs: P08 x5, P18 x6, P02, P11).** No
  mechanism moved the distributors' first counter (5.43 to 5.60 at anchors 0.787 and 0.85, with or
  without claims) or Kalwisz's 45.50; a 40 % share of the gap in round 2 got the same 0.10
  concession as 30 % (P18, two runs). The spread between identical runs decides the best score:
  P08 ended 5.26 (0.648, our new best, `practice-v9.log`), 5.34, 5.42, 5.57 with the same code.
  P02 words registered but the price stayed 372 to 373. → The round-1 counter and the two or
  three capped concessions after it are the supplier's; what we control is to feed every cap
  (25 to 35 % of the gap, never under 1 %, never over 50 %) and never to lose a round.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **v8 (robustness and the reader), no quota spent.** All 21 case files
  (the nine never hosted included) and both sandbox cases play through `arena-sim` with the
  agent and no guarded error (`tests/test_cases.py`). New: every move and setup is guarded (a
  failed move resends our last sheet, a third failure closes the thread on the best standing
  sheet), the final's poll loop never raises and a crashed case is resumed once with its path
  rebuilt from the thread (`Negotiator.restore`), the Sunday release's letters and news reach the
  persona profile through the kit's `ids` and `document`, supplier e-mails are scanned for the
  same traits, quotes and orders priced per 100 or 1000 are compared per piece and cited as
  recorded, an unknown Incoterm or a scorecard without a quarter no longer breaks a move, the
  cost-breakdown question (answered "we do not share" 12 of 12 times) is gone.

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **The price engine (branch `steffen/price-engine`), practice v1 to v6** (47
  sessions): v1 (terms by C, goal anchors, 30 % path, claims) took the mean of best scores from
  0.32 to 0.66; v2 to v6 added mirroring alternatives, overtime valuation, the RFQ scheduler,
  rival offers every round and a model-written paragraph (0.73). What did not help: a patience
  budget for every supplier (P08, P18 fell), a milder anchor for suppliers with a pricing
  committee (P07, P18 fell), currency claims (irrelevant), switching a required index clause to
  a 5 % deadband (refused). Run logs `logs/practice-v1.log` to `-v6.log`, decisions per move in
  `logs/runs/`.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.
